newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia postpones legislation controlling press.
newsitem.headline: Zambia postpones legislation controlling press.

text.p: The Zambian government on Tuesday indefinitely postponed proposed legislation to regulate the press after public and diplomatic pressure.

"In order to allow for further consultation, with all stakeholders and principally the electors, the government has defered the proposed Media Council Bill," Information Minister David Mpamba said in a statement.
Scores of Zambian journalists staged angry protests at the weekend against the proposed law which aims to give government the power to bar journalists from working.
The bill has been condemned as oppressive by international observers, including the Namibian-based Media Institute for Southern Africa (MISA) and the International Federation of Journalists (IFJ).

"There is no reference to the rights of freedom of expression and access to information (in the bill), there is detailed and dangerously wide reference to disciplinary procedures to be taken against journalists," the IFJ said in a statement.
Mpamba accused some foreign diplomats of exerting undue pressure on the government to withdraw the bill.
"It is a matter of profound regret that some diplomats accredited to Zambia have taken it open themselves to issue very crude instructions to the government of the Republic of Zambia," he said.
"Established norms and etiquette dictate that diplomats conduct affairs regarding countries they are accredited to through normal diplomatic channels," he added.
State newspapers reported on Tuesday that the Irish embassy had urged the government to suspend the bill until consensus had been reached with journalists and other interested parties.

The government has been criticised for obstructing press freedom. At least one Zambian journalist has been jailed for contempt of court over an article he wrote criticising the government. Three journalists face court charges for articles they published on the government.

Western donors cut aid to Zambia last year after the government introduced constitutional changes barring some opposition parties from participating in last November's general election, won by President Frederick Chiluba.
